result.title: Target-Constrained Pooling for Trajectory Extrapolation
result.summary: Trajectory extrapolation from a partial target trajectory is underdetermined, but completed related trajectories provide information about the unresolved continuation. We propose target-constrained pooling (TCP), which separates the finite-horizon endpoint from continuation shape and estimates that endpoint from two complementary source signals. Uniform pooling captures final response levels, while matched-increment pooling captures the remaining change after aligning source and target states. TCP selects representative sources, projects both endpoint estimates onto a target-consistent region, converts them into corrections of the free forecast, and controls their influence through strength calibration and degradation-aware weighting. Across 25,245 targets from five domains and both forecasting directions, TCP reduces mean RMSE by 35.8% to 42.1% for all ten target-only forecasters and improves all 100 forecaster, dataset, and direction comparisons. The two endpoint signals consistently outperform either alone, while representative selection remains within 0.64% to 1.02% of the full donor pool using 12.7x fewer donor inputs and 138.8x fewer matching distance computations.

AI.brief_summary: 针对部分轨迹外推的欠定问题，提出目标约束池化（TCP）：将有限视界端点与延续形状分离，用均匀池化与增量匹配池化两路互补信号估计端点，再投影到目标一致区域并以强度校准、退化感知加权修正自由预测；在五个领域、25,245 个目标上验证了 RMSE 下降与代表性筛选的高效性。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 无直接关系，但「用检索到的相关轨迹约束欠定后续状态、并以可靠性加权融合互补估计」的思路，可能为 latent 推理轨迹的外推修正或证据融合提供可供核查的线索。
